thread:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - Elevated error rate from prod inference fleet. Service: /v1/generate — 500s up ~15% over baseline. Paging Aisha (eng-oncall) and oncall rotation.

Aisha (eng-oncall): saw the alert, paging in. Pulling dashboards now.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: release v2026.11 -> canary group 3 (pods: inference-rc-3). image=registry.redwood.dev/inference/service:canary-202611-g12345.

Tara (sre): slack: I'm seeing spikes in 5xx for canary pods only, latency up too. Canary pods show OOM+restart traces in kube events.

Aisha (eng-oncall): OK hold the rollout. @deploy-bot pause-rollout canary-group=3 — please confirm paused.

deploy-bot: Rollout pause ACKed for canary group 3.

Marco (infra): grabbing logs from the canary pod. quick check: image reported in pod status is registry.redwood.dev/inference/service:latest (digest: sha256:deadbeef1234), but CI artifact digest for canary-202611-g12345 is sha256:feedface9876. That mismatch looks off.

Aisha (eng-oncall): wait, how did latest get into canary? CI should have pinned canary tag. run: kubectl describe pod inference-canary-3 | grep Image

Tara (sre): pasted output:

```
> Containers:
>   inference:
>     Image: registry.redwood.dev/inference/service:latest
>     Image ID: docker-pullable://...@sha256:deadbeef1234
```

Aisha (eng-oncall): that suggests the image tag 'latest' got re-pointed after the canary created -> BAD. Could be artifact cache or tag overwrite in CI.

Marco (infra): checked CI artifact registry logs: at 12:02 UTC a retry of a previous pipeline re-tagged 'latest' with a different digest due to a caching bug in artifact-uploader. Evidence: upload log snippet:

```
2026-11-08T12:02:11Z uploader: overwriting tag 'latest' -> digest=sha256:deadbeef1234 (prev=sha256:feedface9876) -- retry path
```

Aisha (eng-oncall): OK impact: canary traffic is routed to wrong image causing failures. Need immediate mitigation: 1) apply feature-flag kill-switch to stop routing prod traffic to canary; 2) revert image tag on canary pods to pinned digest OR roll back deployment; 3) notify SRE and customers if high impact.

Tara (sre): I can flip the FF. Feature flags service endpoint:
`POST https://flags.redwood.dev/toggle` body `{ "flag": "route_canary_v2", "enabled": false }`

Aisha (eng-oncall): Tara go ahead. I'll prepare rollback commands.

Tara (sre): done :white_check_mark: Response 200, flag route_canary_v2=false. Traffic to canary should drop within ~10s. Watching metrics.

deploy-bot: Canary traffic drain in progress. Current canary QPS -> 2% of baseline.

Marco (infra): Applying rollback to canary group -> pin to digest sha256:feedface9876 (the intended canary image). Command: `kubectl set image deployment/inference --container=inference=registry.redwood.dev/inference/service@sha256:feedface9876 --record`

Aisha (eng-oncall): run the set-image on canary replicas first and restart pods. Use `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference --selector=canary=3` after set-image.

Marco (infra): running now. paste logs:

```
deployment.apps/inference image updated
rolling restart triggered
pod/inference-canary-3-abcde terminating
pod/inference-canary-3-fghij pulling image sha256:feedface9876
pod/inference-canary-3-fghij started
```

Tara (sre): metrics: 5xxs falling back to baseline, latency normalizing. No new OOMs.

Aisha (eng-oncall): Good. Now we need to assess customer impact. Quick numbers: from dashboards, error spike lasted ~8 minutes, peak +15% 5xx across region-us-west-2, estimated affected requests ~12k, unique API keys touched ~14. No major enterprise customers flagged yet.

Aisha (eng-oncall): tagging #support to check customer-reported errors and to prep comms if any paying customers hit.

ops-rotation: I'm taking the handoff in 20 minutes. Documenting actions: paused rollout, feature-flag kill-switch turned off, pinned canary to intended digest, rolled canary pods, monitoring ok. Postmortem owners: Marco infra (artifact uploader), Tara SRE (mitigation), Aisha (incident lead).

Tara (sre): note for postmortem: CI uploader should never overwrite stable tags on retry. We need immutability or write-locks and a retry backoff fix.

Marco (infra): I'll open a ticket in infra-tracking with logs and a patch proposal to add tag immutability and an artifact cache flush.

Aisha (eng-oncall): Handing off to Marco. I'll stay available for questions but my shift ends in 18m. Please escalate to oncall rotation if error rates rise.

Marco (infra): acknowledged. Creating ticket RDW-ART-4321 and assigning to infra. Summary in ticket: "artifact-uploader retry overwrote 'latest' tag -> bad canary image". Adding rollback steps and customer impact notes.

deploy-bot: incident action logged: pause-rollout, toggle-flag, set-image, restart-rollout. Duration ~00:12:40 from first alert to traffic normalized.

Aisha (eng-oncall): closing the real-time incident thread but keeping this thread open for the postmortem draft. Great work everyone. :thumbsup:
